title: Rivet: the reigning saints pray in general for the Church still fighting
source_text: XLVII. Alii vero non gravate concedunt, & probabile existimant Sanctos in caelis cum Christo regnantes, in genere saltem pro Ecclesia hic pugnante orare: quoniam id videtur plane consentaneum & charitati qua fervent, & communioni quae est inter utramque Ecclesiam, Militantem atque Triumphantem. Sic ea de re sententiam suam exponit Andreas Rivetus. Non negamus, inquit, Sanctorum Ecclesiam cum Christo regnantem, de membris hic pugnantibus esse sollicitam. Sed ea cura est communis, non ex cujusque conditionis notitia, sed ex generali eorum scientia, qua norunt quod, cum tota Ecclesia nondum sit recepta ubi regnant, semper aliqui militent in terra, pro quorum conservatione ac complemento, eos Deum precari, ut ejus regni incrementum semper petunt, non dubitamus. Summa controversiarum tractatu secundo, quaest. 48.
pass_a_gloss: But others concede without reluctance, and judge it probable, that the Saints reigning with Christ in heaven pray at least in general for the Church fighting here: since that seems plainly consonant both with the charity with which they burn, and with the communion which is between both Churches, the Militant and the Triumphant. So Andrew Rivet sets out his opinion on that matter. We do not deny, he says, that the Church of the Saints reigning with Christ is anxious about the members fighting here. But that care is common, not from the knowledge of each one's condition, but from their general knowledge, by which they know that, since the whole Church has not yet been received where they reign, some always fight on earth, for whose preservation and completion we do not doubt that they pray to God, as they always ask for the increase of his kingdom. Summary of Controversies, second treatise, question 48.
pass_b_english: Others readily grant, and think it probable, that the saints reigning with Christ in heaven pray at least in general for the Church fighting here, since this seems wholly in keeping with the love that burns in them and with the communion between the two Churches, the Church Militant and the Church Triumphant.

Andrew Rivet states his view this way: "We do not deny that the Church of the saints who reign with Christ cares for the members still fighting here. But that care is general. It does not come from knowing each person's condition but from their general knowledge: they know that the whole Church has not yet been received where they reign, and that some are always fighting on earth. We do not doubt that they pray to God for the preservation and completion of these, just as they always ask for the growth of his kingdom." (Summary of Controversies, second treatise, question 48.)

choices.why: Rivet contrasts a care for the whole Church with knowledge of individual cases; 'general' carries that contrast.
